Handle the rejected destroy promise with popupAjaxError (or equivalent) before removing the host from the list. When the DELETE fails, the rejection is left unhandled and the user receives no error feedback, so the UI can remain out of sync with the server.

This deletes the original *_ids field even when _lookupSubType cannot resolve one or more IDs. Since _lookupSubType explicitly returns undefined when the root response has no matching collection/record, a partial or non-embedded response becomes a relationship containing undefined entries.
A PUT for a nonexistent :id reaches save_host(nil) and raises NoMethodError when it assigns host.host, returning a 500 instead of the controller's normal not-found response.
When :id does not match a row, host is nil and host.destroy raises NoMethodError. This makes DELETE of an unknown resource return 500 rather than a consistent not-found response.

Missing embeddable_host[host] input causes this assignment to leave host.host nil, and EmbeddableHost's before_validation callback unconditionally calls self.host.sub!. Malformed create/update requests raise NoMethodError and return 500 instead of the normal validation error response.
Submitting an embeddable host without a host value raises NoMethodError during validation instead of returning a validation error. The before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! on nil.

This comparison lowercases only the stored column, not the parsed host value. Since URI parsing preserves the case of a hostname and the model validation allows uppercase hostnames, EXAMPLE.COM will not match a stored example.com.

The lookup discards the port from the incoming URI (uri.host returns only the hostname), while the validation explicitly permits and the normalization callback preserves :port in the stored value. A host entered as example.com:8080 can be saved but can never match a referer.

When a Discover query contains event.type:error alongside transaction terms, or negates that term, _is_error_focused_query returns true from substring match, causing organization_events_stats to rewrite count() for rows that are not errors and can upsample zero error matches. Need to parse the query or require a positive error-only event-type constraint before enabling the transformation.

When organization_events_stats calls _get_event_stats with a derived query such as transactions_only_query, _should_apply_sample_weight_transform inspects request.GET instead of that effective query, so an original event.type:error request enables upsampling for the derived transaction query. The split response then reports transaction counts using error sample weights.

When a caller submits upsampled_count() directly on the Discover dataset, DiscoverDatasetConfig exposes this internal helper as a public function, so Snuba attempts sum(sample_weight) for non-allowlisted or transaction events where that column is not available and the request fails. The function should be marked private=True so only the controlled rewrite can invoke it.

When store_event receives an error-sampling context with a non-numeric or out-of-range rate, _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling still writes a converted sample_rate, so test-created events are persisted with an invalid sampling weight and can produce incorrect upsampled counts. Need to apply the same type and range validation as event_manager._derive_client_error_sampling_rate which accepts only numeric values in (0, 1].

Upsampling eligibility uses outer dataset and raw request query instead of scoped values. When _get_event_stats runs for a split dashboard widget or a discover/transactions split, it passes the outer dataset and the raw request to is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects, but the query actually executed uses scoped_dataset and the rewritten query.

60s eligibility cache serves stale allowlist decisions and contradicts the function's own docstring. When issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist changes, is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects keeps returning the cached error_upsampling_eligible:{org}:{hash} value for up to 60s. A project removed from the allowlist keeps getting upsampled_count() until the entry expires.

count() rewrite assumes sample_weight is always populated. When an allowlisted project has events stored without sample_weight (older events or events with no client sample rate), transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling rewrites count() to upsampled_count() as count, which resolves to toInt64(sum(sample_weight)) returning 0 or NULL for those rows, showing lower counts in charts.

When handleEnable succeeds and setStep(SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes) runs, dismissing the dialog through onOpenChange closes the modal without calling onEnable, so the server has enabled 2FA while the only plaintext backup codes are discarded from the user's view. Make this success step non-dismissible until onEnable runs, or handle every close path by explicitly preserving/revealing or regenerating the codes.

When two login requests use the same backup code concurrently, authorize reads the same list before either update and both requests pass the match, so the single-use code authenticates twice. The later prisma.user.update also overwrites the earlier list from its stale snapshot. Consume the code with an atomic compare-and-set (or serialize the read/claim/update in a transaction) before accepting either login.

Backup code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write, so one code can be reused. Two concurrent authorize calls with the same backup code can both read the same decrypted user.backupCodes list and both find the code at index. Each then writes back its own copy with only that slot nulled, so both logins succeed and the single-use guarantee fails.
Credential-named variable assigned a 16+ char hardcoded literal.

When the browser denies clipboard access or navigator.clipboard is unavailable, this handler invokes writeText without awaiting or catching its rejection, but immediately shows backup_codes_copied, so users can believe their recovery codes were saved when they were not. Await the clipboard operation inside try/catch and show an error or fallback instruction on failure.

When the modal is closed after entering a six-digit code, resetState leaves form's totpCode registered, so useEffect sees the old six-digit value on the next setup and handleEnable submits it before the user reaches the OTP step. This can attempt enabling 2FA with a stale code and show an error in a hidden step. Reset totpCode (and unregister/reset the form) in resetState.

When TypeScript infers the empty array initializer, backupCodes becomes never[], so setBackupCodes(body.backupCodes) is not assignable and the web package fails type-checking/building. Declare the state with the actual backup-code element type (for example useState<string[]>([])) before storing the API response.

When a 2FA-enabled user authenticated through a non-CAL identity provider submits a backup code, authorize rejects the request in the earlier !credentials.totpCode identity-provider guards before reaching this branch, so backup codes cannot recover access for those users. Update those guards to treat credentials.backupCode as a valid second factor, or validate the backup-code path before the provider-specific TOTP checks.

When a keyboard user tabs through a PasswordField, the visibility button is removed from the tab sequence, so they cannot reach or activate the control without a mouse and the password visibility toggle fails the keyboard-operability contract. Remove tabIndex={-1} or set it to 0 so the button remains keyboard accessible.

Backup codes can be lost, and stay in state, if the dialog closes without the Close button. When handleEnable succeeds, 2FA is already enabled on the server and setStep(DisplayBackupCodes) is the only time the codes are shown. The Dialog still receives onOpenChange, so Escape or a click outside closes it without calling resetState or onEnable.

When a paid collective booking reaches handlePaymentSuccess, this event contains only booking.destinationCalendar or the organizer's calendar, so EventManager.create never receives the other hosts' calendars and they are not invited. handleNewBooking stores only the first destination while keeping the team list only on the in-memory event. Persist or reload all collective host calendars before constructing this payment event.

When getBooking or handlePaymentSuccess reconstructs a paid collective booking, selectedDestinationCalendar contains only the persisted primary calendar or organizer fallback, so EventManager.create cannot invite the other hosts. handleNewBooking stores only evt.destinationCalendar[0], not the appended team calendars. Persist or reload all collective host calendars before building either event.

When IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is false, createHandler omits both slug and requestedSlug, so the newly created organization has no usable URL and publishHandler cannot recover it because it requires metadata.requestedSlug. This breaks self-hosted organization creation. Restore the non-billing branch for slug while retaining requestedSlug only for billing-enabled organizations.

When a collective booking requires confirmation, confirmHandler rebuilds evt.destinationCalendar from only the persisted booking destination or the confirming user's calendar, so handleConfirmation creates an event for at most one host and omits the other collective hosts collected by handleNewBooking. Confirming such a booking leaves those hosts without calendar events; load the collective event members' destination calendars before calling handleConfirmation.

When a booking has multiple Lark destinations, EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents invokes createEvent once per destination credential but LarkCalendarService.createEvent always selects event.destinationCalendar[0], so the second host's event is sent to the first host's calendar (or fails because that calendar is not visible to the second account). Use the destination matching the active credential, or pass the selected external calendar ID into this service.

When evt.destinationCalendar is an empty array, EventManager.create dereferences mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration, so event creation throws before the intended Meet fallback runs. Use optional chaining (or explicitly handle the empty list) so a missing destination safely selects Cal Video instead of producing an unhandled booking failure.

When a reschedule merges a booking with multiple calendar references, updateAllCalendarEvents updates every new reference but the existing cleanup below still deletes only the first old calendar reference, so the other hosts' old events remain active and attendees see duplicate/stale bookings. Delete every old calendar reference after processing the new references, rather than selecting one with find.

When cancelling a recurring booking with multiple calendar references, handleCancelBooking runs every credential against updBooking.references.find(...), so each calendar adapter receives the first calendar reference's UID and external ID rather than its matching credential reference. Secondary events can remain active, or the wrong provider can be asked to delete them. Match each booking reference to the current credential (or iterate the references directly) before calling deleteEvent.

When EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents processes a secondary destination with a different credential, BaseCalendarService.createEvent filters that credential's calendars using the first destination's externalId, so it produces no iCal event for the secondary host (or targets the wrong calendar when IDs overlap). Use the destination matching the current credential, passed through the credentialId parameter, or avoid filtering when no matching destination exists.

When evt.destinationCalendar is null or [], const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = ... ?? [] leaves it undefined. mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration then throws a TypeError, so create() crashes for a Google Meet event with no destination calendar. The old code used ?.

In create(), credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined replaces the old isCalendarType ? destinationCalendar?.credentialId : result.credentialId. For video results (Daily, Zoom, Meet) the credentialId is now always undefined, so the saved booking reference has no credential. Later reschedule or cancel can no longer resolve the video.

The fallback only runs when externalCalendarId is falsy. find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId) therefore compares against a falsy value and always yields undefined. updateEvent ends up with no calendar id. deleteEvent (line 317) has the identical bug and falls back to primary.

createEvent always uses event.destinationCalendar[0].externalId. EventManager now calls createEvent once per destination and credential, so a second collective host's Office365 credential posts to /me/calendars/<first host's calendar id>/events. The calendar does not exist for that user, so the request fails or lands in the wrong calendar.

evt.destinationCalendar is null when neither eventType.destinationCalendar nor organizerUser.destinationCalendar exists. evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars) is then a no-op. Collective hosts' calendars are never added, so those hosts get no calendar event. Initialise the array to [] and always push the team calendars.

The old code set slug only when !IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED. The new IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {} sets it only when billing is enabled. With billing on, the slug is now created immediately and also stored as requestedSlug. With billing off, no slug is set at all.

When a booking has a Meet location but neither it nor its user has a destination calendar, confirmHandler supplies an empty array, so EventManager.create reaches mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration and throws instead of creating the configured fallback meeting or calendar event. Preserve a nullable/missing value or guard the first destination before reading integration.

When a destination has no matching credentialId (for example, the existing no-credential destination path), createEvent inserts into primary but the hangout-link patch uses selectedCalendar as undefined, so Google rejects the patch and the created event keeps the incomplete description. Preserve the same fallback calendar ID for both insert and patch, or skip the patch when no ID is available.

When updateEvent is called without an externalCalendarId, this lookup searches for a destination whose externalId equals undefined, so it always returns undefined instead of the event's main destination calendar. The subsequent Google update therefore receives an invalid calendar ID and rescheduling fails on callers that omit the external ID. Use the first destination as the fallback.

When deleteEvent is called without an externalCalendarId, this lookup compares every destination ID with undefined, yielding no calendar ID and forcing deletion on primary. For a non-primary configured destination, Google returns 404 and the stale event remains there. Fall back to the first destination calendar when no explicit external ID is supplied.

When createEvent is invoked for the second collective host, mainHostDestinationCalendar still selects the first destination while selectedCalendar selects the current credential's destination, so the event on host 2's calendar is created with host 1's calendar ID as the organizer attendee and Google can assign the wrong organizer/invitation identity. Select the destination matching credentialId for the attendee as well.

When a collective booking is rescheduled through updateEvent for a non-first destination, mainHostDestinationCalendar still comes from index 0 even though the update receives that destination's externalCalendarId, so the updated event sends the first host's calendar identity as its organizer attendee. Match this value by externalCalendarId, with the first destination only as the fallback for legacy events.

When a destination has no credentialId, this branch calls createEvent without destination.externalId, so its EventResult.externalId is undefined even though the destination selected a specific external calendar. EventManager.create then persists that missing value in referencesToCreate, leaving cancellation or rescheduling unable to address the selected provider calendar. Pass the destination external ID through this branch too.

When updateLocation rebuilds references, result.externalId is always absent for updateEvent: CalendarManager.updateEvent returns no externalId field. Consequently this mapping overwrites each existing externalCalendarId with undefined, and a later cancellation or reschedule cannot target the provider event. Preserve the reference's existing external ID or return it from updateEvent.

When a reference's credentialId is missing from both the in-memory list and Prisma, this line calls updateEvent with undefined; CalendarManager.updateEvent then returns by reading credential.appName, which rejects. The surrounding Promise.all catch converts the whole update into generic failures, masking valid references that were already processed. Skip or record only this reference when no credential can be loaded.

When a recurring booking reference is recovered by the prisma.credential.findUnique fallback, this branch still builds its deletion work only from bookingToDelete.user.credentials, so calendarCredential is never used for recurring deletion. If the referenced credential is absent from the eager relation, its recurring events are not deleted. Include the recovered credential in the deletion set or delete through the matched reference directly.

When a recurring booking has multiple calendar references, handleCancelBooking enters the all-credentials recurring deletion block once per outer reference, and each entry loops over all credentials and all updatedBookings. The same external events are therefore submitted for deletion repeatedly, which can produce provider errors and makes cancellation dependent on duplicate requests. Move recurring deletion outside the per-reference loop or scope it to the matched reference and credential.

When a collective event type has an explicit eventType.destinationCalendar, handleNewBooking makes it the only primary calendar and never adds the first selected host's user.destinationCalendar, so that host's calendar event is omitted while later hosts are appended. Build the list from all collective hosts (deduplicating the configured primary if appropriate), or otherwise explicitly guarantee that this calendar belongs to the first host.

When the organizer and event type have no destination calendar but a later collective host does, this optional push discards every teamDestinationCalendars entry because evt.destinationCalendar is null. The booking then reaches EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents without any destination and falls back to the organizer's connected calendar, so the host calendar is not created. Initialize the event array from teamDestinationCalendars when no primary exists, or concatenate before assigning evt.destinationCalendar.

When any non-SMS workflow reminder has retryCount > 1, this handler deletes it as well, so email or other-method reminders are permanently lost during the SMS cron run. The retry cleanup must remain scoped to SMS reminders by adding method: WorkflowMethods.SMS to the second OR branch, or by combining the method predicate outside the OR.

When two cron requests process the same unscheduled reminder concurrently, both scheduleSMSReminders iterations read the same reminder.retryCount and write the same incremented value, so the failure count is lost and the reminder can be sent/retried beyond the two-failure limit. Use Prisma's atomic increment: 1 update and add a claim/lock before scheduling to prevent concurrent processing.

retryCount is a counter that must remain non-negative, but this migration permits arbitrary negative values. A negative value would never satisfy the cleanup predicate (retryCount > 1) and could leave a failed reminder retained indefinitely if written by another client or an administrative update. Add a CHECK ("retryCount" >= 0) constraint when introducing the column.

Unguarded retryCount update in catch can abort the whole cron run - when twilio.scheduleSMS or a prior step throws and the prisma.workflowReminder.update in the catch block also throws, the exception escapes the loop causing a 500 error and preventing processing of later reminders.

Retry count is not incremented when message or sendTo is missing - when sendTo is empty or message is empty, the if block is skipped, no exception is thrown, and the reminder stays scheduled: false and is retried on every cron run until scheduledDate.

Failure after a successful scheduleSMS is counted as a retry and can cause a duplicate SMS - when twilio.scheduleSMS succeeds but the following update setting scheduled: true throws, the catch block increments retryCount and the reminder remains scheduled: false, causing the next cron run to schedule the same SMS again.

When the cron runs after a cancelled reminder's scheduled date, the earlier unconditional deleteMany removes the row before this sweep can call SendGrid, so the provider send remains active and the cancelled email is delivered. Exclude cancelled: true from the expiry cleanup or perform provider cancellation before deleting past-due rows.

When a workflow with scheduled email reminders is deleted, deleteScheduledEmailReminder runs without await and workflow.deleteMany executes immediately, so the mutation can finish while the SendGrid cancellation is still pending; a provider failure is only logged by the helper and the scheduled email can still be sent. Await all cancellation calls before deleting the workflow.

When an edited step has reminders in remindersToUpdate, this forEach(async ...) is not awaited by the surrounding workflow update, so reminder cancellation continues after new reminders are created and the mutation can report success with the old scheduled send still active. Replace it with an awaited Promise.all (and propagate cancellation failures) before scheduling replacements.

When a cancelled or rescheduled booking reaches the next cron run after its email scheduledDate, deleteScheduledEmailReminder only marks the reminder cancelled, while scheduleEmailReminders deletes all past email rows before processing cancelled rows. The SendGrid batch therefore remains active and the reminder is sent. Exclude cancelled rows from the initial past-date deletion or cancel them before deleting expired rows.

When a booking is rescheduled, this forEach starts the asynchronous cancellation calls without awaiting them, so handleNewBooking proceeds to eventManager.reschedule and can return before the provider cancellation completes; a failed or delayed call can leave the old reminder active and it can still be sent. Replace the loop with an awaited Promise.all (and make failures observable) before rescheduling.

When a booking is cancelled, these asynchronous reminder cancellations are launched without being awaited, so the handler can finish and the serverless process can be reclaimed before workflowReminder.cancelled is persisted or the SMS provider is cancelled. The reminder then remains active and can be sent. Collect these promises and await them before returning, or use an explicit durable job.

Reschedule cancels email reminders immediately, bringing back the 100-pending-cancellation failure. When a booking is rescheduled, deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true) posts a SendGrid cancel straight away and returns. It never sets cancelled=true and never deletes the row.

When SendGrid rejects cancellation for one reminder, this loop aborts before deleting or processing the remaining reminders, so eligible cancelled emails remain in the database and are retried as a blocked batch on every run. Process each reminder in its own try/catch (and delete only after its request succeeds), or use per-item settled results so one invalid batch ID does not stop the cron sweep.

When a booking is rescheduled, these cancellation calls are launched without awaiting them, so the mutation can finish while workflowReminder.cancelled is still false; the reminder scheduler can then select the old reminder and send it. Await the cancellation promises (for example, collect them and await Promise.all) before continuing.

When immediateDelete is true during rescheduling, deleteScheduledEmailReminder cancels SendGrid and returns without deleting or marking the WorkflowReminder, so the old booking retains a scheduled reminder that is neither represented as cancelled nor recoverable by the cancellation sweep. Delete the row after a successful immediate cancellation, or mark it cancelled so stale records are reconciled.

try/catch cannot catch failures from un-awaited async reminder deletes. deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are async, and they are called inside forEach without await. The surrounding try/catch therefore catches nothing, and log.error is dead. The promises are floating.

Reminder cancellation is no longer awaited on the booking-cancel path. Before this change, the reminder deleteMany calls were awaited through Promise.all(prismaPromises...). Now deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are fired inside updatedBookings.forEach and never awaited.

SMS reminder row is kept when the Twilio cancel throws. When twilio.cancelSMS(referenceId) throws, the catch block logs and returns before prisma.workflowReminder.delete runs. The row stays behind for a cancelled booking and nothing retries it, so the SMS can still go out. Delete the row in a finally, or in an independent step.

One failed SendGrid cancel aborts the whole cancellation batch and skips all row deletions. The loop awaits client.request for each reminder. The deletes are queued in workflowRemindersToDelete and only run in Promise.all after the loop. When one cancel call throws, the catch exits the loop. The remaining cancelled reminders are not cancelled.

When a date override spans a daylight-saving transition, getSlots applies the UTC-offset difference at override.start to both endpoints, so the converted endTime is wrong after the organizer or invitee changes offset during the override
Date-override bounds check only rejects a slot whose start is after the override end, but a slot that starts inside the override but ends after it is still accepted

When --flusher-processes is set to a negative value, SpanFlusher computes a negative num_processes and then hits modulo by -1 while assigning shards, causing the consumer to fail during startup; 0 also silently means all shards because of the or fallback

When more than one batch is needed, CleanAnnotations applies the same LIMIT ... Integration test only checks final row counts, so it would still pass if cleanup reverted to the original subquery-based DELETE. SQLite does not reproduce the concurrent MySQL deadlock that motivates this change, and this test creates no concurrent writer or assertion on the separate fetch/delete operations; a regression in the split-query behavior therefore passes CI.

The 40,003 fixtures are distributed across the three annotation types, so each cleanup query receives only about 13,334 IDs. That is below SQLite >= 3.32's 32,766/32,767-variable limit. Consequently, replacing the literal-ID workaround with a placeholder list would still pass, so the claimed variable-limit regression is not exercised.

When SQLite is configured with a very large AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize, deleteByIDs interpolates every fetched ID into one IN statement, while readAnnotationSettings accepts any positive int64 and the documented setting has no upper bound. A sufficiently large batch exceeds SQLite's SQL length/parser limits, so cleanup errors or exhausts memory instead of progressing.

When AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize exceeds the database driver's parameter limit on MSSQL (2100) or PostgreSQL/MySQL (typically 65535), deleteByIDs sends one placeholder per fetched ID and the delete fails with a bind/parameter-count error. Cleanup then stops with an error instead of deleting the configured batch.

When clean takes longer than one minute, time.Ticker queues a tick while the synchronous cleanup is running, so Run starts the next clean immediately after the prior one returns. Because each run has a nine-minute timeout and includes database cleanup jobs, sustained slow work makes cleanup runs effectively back-to-back and adds avoidable database load.

Cleanup ticker interval cut from 10 minutes to 1 minute, which changes the schedule for every cleanup job, not only annotations. That includes temp files, expired sessions, and the annotation cleanup. Cleanup then runs 10 times as often, which adds database load.
